content: The recommended dosage of cefixime for adults is 400 mg daily. This can be administered as a single 400 mg tablet or capsule once daily, or the 400 mg tablet may be split and given as one-half tablet every 12 hours. For the treatment of uncomplicated cervical or urethral gonococcal infections, a single oral dose of 400 mg is recommended. Cefixime tablets and capsules can be taken with or without food. In cases of infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes, cefixime should be administered at a therapeutic dosage for a minimum of 10 days. For pediatric patients aged 6 months or older, the recommended dose is 8 mg/kg/day of the suspension. This can be given as a single daily dose or divided into two doses of 4 mg/kg every 12 hours. It is important to note that a suggested dose has been determined for each pediatric weight range. When prescribing doses in milliliters, the concentration must be specified, as Suprax oral suspension is available in three different concentrations: 100 mg/5 mL, 200 mg/5 mL, and 500 mg/5 mL. Children weighing more than 45 kg or older than 12 years should receive the recommended adult dose. Suprax chewable tablets must be chewed or crushed before swallowing. Otitis media should be treated with the chewable tablets or suspension, as clinical trials for otitis media were conducted using these forms. The chewable tablets or suspension result in higher peak blood levels compared to the tablet when administered at the same dose. Therefore, the tablet or capsule should not be substituted for the chewable tablets or suspension in the treatment of otitis media. For infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes, cefixime should be administered at a therapeutic dosage for at least 10 days. In patients with renal impairment, Suprax can be administered. The normal dose and schedule may be used in patients with creatinine clearances of 60 mL/min or greater. Dose adjustments for adults with renal impairment should be made according to specific guidelines. Neither hemodialysis nor peritoneal dialysis removes significant amounts of the drug from the body. After reconstitution, the oral suspension can be stored for up to 14 days at room temperature or under refrigeration without significant loss of potency. The bottle should be kept tightly closed, shaken well before use, and any unused portion should be discarded after 14 days.
